tasks.title: Filter out zero-point leagues from expected wins and trends calculations
tasks.description: Bug: On /expected-wins/trends, user 'edgecdec' shows 2020 with 0% actual win rate and ~50% expected win rate. This is caused by a league where the user scored 0 total points (likely a test league or a league where the regular season never happened). The matchup data exists with 0-point entries, so totalOpportunities > 0 passes the current filter, and expected wins calculate to ~50% because ties with other 0-point teams count as 0.5. Fix: In src/services/stats/expectedWins.ts, after calculating a user's stats in analyzeLeague(), treat a team with 0 total pointsFor as having no valid data — return userStats as undefined so the league is excluded from aggregation. This fix will apply globally to all pages using analyzeLeague() (the main expected-wins page, trends, and league-history views). Verify by checking that 2020 no longer appears in the trends chart for edgecdec.

tasks.title: Add 50% average reference line to luck trends chart
tasks.description: On /expected-wins/trends, add a horizontal dashed line at 50% on the Y axis to indicate where the average player would be. Use Recharts ReferenceLine component with y={50}, a gray stroke, dashed strokeDasharray, and a label like 'Average'. This gives visual context for whether the user is performing above or below the league median over time.

tasks.title: Show Draft Assistant for edgecdec user instead of dev-only
tasks.description: In src/components/layout/AppLayout.tsx, the Draft Assistant nav item is currently gated behind process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'. Change this so it is instead shown when the logged-in Sleeper user is 'edgecdec'. Use the existing useUser() hook to get the current user and check user.username === 'edgecdec'. The MENU_ITEMS list should be computed dynamically (e.g. via useMemo) rather than at module scope, since it now depends on runtime user state. Remove the NODE_ENV check entirely.

tasks.title: Ensure 50% reference line is always visible on luck trends chart
tasks.description: Bug: The 50% dashed reference line added in TASK-002 is not visible when all data points are above or below 50%, because the YAxis domain is set to auto and Recharts clips the chart to the data range. Fix: In src/app/expected-wins/trends/page.tsx, change the YAxis domain so it always includes 50. For example, use a domain function like domain={[dataMin => Math.min(dataMin, 48), dataMax => Math.max(dataMax, 52)]} to ensure the 50% line is always within the visible area with a small buffer. Do NOT hardcode 0-100 — the axis should still auto-scale to the data, just guaranteed to include the 50% mark.

tasks.title: Exclude already-rostered players from draft assistant in dynasty leagues
tasks.description: In dynasty leagues, most players are already rostered from previous seasons and are NOT in the draft pool — only rookies and free agents are draftable. Currently BestAvailable (src/components/draft/BestAvailable.tsx) only filters out players picked in the current draft via the picks array. Fix: When a draft is selected in src/app/draft-assistant/page.tsx, use the draft's league_id to fetch all rosters via SleeperService.getRosters(league_id). Collect every player_id from all rosters' 'players' arrays into a Set of rostered player IDs. Pass this Set (or array) as a new prop 'rosteredPlayerIds' to BestAvailable. In BestAvailable, filter out both drafted picks AND rostered players from the available pool. This should only apply when the league is a dynasty/keeper league — check the league settings (fetch the league via SleeperService.getLeague(league_id) and check if settings.type === 2 for dynasty, or if the draft has keeper picks). If it's a redraft league (type 0), skip the roster fetch since all players are available. Also display a small indicator in the UI (e.g. a Chip or subtitle) showing whether the draft is 'Dynasty' or 'Redraft' so the user knows the filtering is active.

tasks.title: Show traded pick ownership in draft assistant
tasks.description: In dynasty leagues, draft picks can be traded between owners. The Sleeper API provides GET /league/{league_id}/traded_picks which returns an array of objects with season, round, roster_id (original owner), owner_id (current owner after trade), and previous_owner_id. Similarly GET /draft/{draft_id}/traded_picks returns traded picks for a specific draft. When a draft is selected in the draft assistant, fetch the traded picks data and build a mapping of which roster_id actually owns each pick. Display this in the DraftBoard component — for each pick slot, show the actual owner (not just the original drafter). This is critical for dynasty leagues like 'Graham's Football Fantasy' where edgecdec has acquired extra picks via trades. The user should be able to see at a glance which picks they own across all rounds, including picks traded from other teams. Add a visual indicator (e.g. highlight or badge) on picks owned by the current user that were acquired via trade.

tasks.title: Add deterministic league-based URLs for draft assistant
tasks.description: Currently the draft assistant lives at /draft-assistant with no URL state — selecting a draft is ephemeral. Add a route /draft-assistant/[leagueId] that deep-links directly to a specific league's draft. When a user selects a draft from the list on /draft-assistant, navigate to /draft-assistant/{league_id}. The [leagueId] page should auto-fetch the league's drafts and select the most relevant one (active 'drafting' first, then 'pre_draft', then most recent 'complete'). This allows bookmarking and sharing direct links to a league's draft view. Create src/app/draft-assistant/[leagueId]/page.tsx as a new route. The existing /draft-assistant/page.tsx remains as the search/discovery page.
